summary: An excerpt from Book 11 (part 111) of a novel, set at Wareham. Adam Ladd, who is fond of the schoolgirl Rebecca, notices she is overworked and pale after a tearful exchange with him at the seminary gate. He then meets the principal, Mr. Morrison, to propose English composition prizes marking the school's fiftieth anniversary, alongside a gift of a hundred volumes to the reference library. Afterward he visits Miss Maxwell, who plans to take Rebecca South for the spring vacation, and Adam offers to share the cost and responsibility.
one_line: At Wareham, Adam Ladd plans anniversary writing prizes and arranges with Miss Maxwell to take the overworked Rebecca South for spring vacation.
key_facts: Adam Ladd tells Rebecca that vacation comes soon and asks whether she will rest and recover her dimples.
Rebecca replies that it is not one of her dimply days and runs into the seminary gate.
This year is the fiftieth anniversary of the founding of the Wareham schools.
Adam intends to give a hundred volumes to the reference library along with the prizes.
Adam plans prizes in English composition for the two upper classes, awarded to the writers of the two best essays.
The prizes will be substantial, either money or books, and Adam has not yet decided which.
Adam thinks Rose-Red-Snow-White needs help but cannot give it without causing remark, so she must earn it.
Miss Maxwell goes South every spring vacation, traveling by sea to Old Point Comfort.
Miss Maxwell considers taking Rebecca with her as a companion on the spring trip.
Adam offers to help Miss Maxwell take Rebecca away, saying he has been interested in the child for some years.
Miss Maxwell says she discovered Rebecca herself.
Adam says he was an intimate friend of Rebecca long before Miss Maxwell came to Wareham.
Miss Maxwell says Rebecca is independent of everything and everybody in a sense.
